title: Exact Mirror-Parity Selection Rule for Electron-Phonon Coupling in Two-Dimensional Crystals
summary: The electron--phonon (e-ph) interaction underlies conventional superconductivity and plays a central role in transport and other many-body phenomena in solids. Here, we derive a symmetry selection rule for e-ph scattering in two-dimensional crystals possessing a horizontal mirror plane, $σ_h$. For electronic states of mirror parity $s_n(\mathbf{k})$ and $s_m(\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{q})$, and a phonon mode of parity $χ_ν(\mathbf{q})$, we show that the e-ph matrix element $g_{mn,ν}(\mathbf{k},\mathbf{q})$ vanishes identically unless $s_n(\mathbf{k})\,χ_ν(\mathbf{q})\, s_m(\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{q})=+1$. The rule follows from the covariance of the phonon-induced deformation potential under $σ_h$, constitutes the $C_s$ case of the general group-theoretical selection rule for matrix elements, and partitions the e-ph interaction throughout the Brillouin zone into symmetry-allowed and symmetry-forbidden scattering channels. Consequently, mirror-even phonons couple electronic states of the same mirror parity, either even--even or odd--odd, whereas mirror-odd phonons couple only states of opposite mirror parity, for both intra- and interband processes. We illustrate the selection rule through first-principles calculations for the two-dimensional superconductor $\mathrm{Sc_2BCH_4}$, where mirror parity is well defined throughout the entire Brillouin zone and symmetry-forbidden matrix elements vanish up to numerical precision. We then extend the analysis to bulk $\mathrm{MgB_2}$, where the rule applies exactly only on mirror-invariant planes of the three-dimensional Brillouin zone. Moving away from these planes removes the exact mirror constraint and activates scattering channels that are symmetry forbidden when the mirror eigenvalues are well defined. Our results establish horizontal mirror symmetry as an exact and practical filter of e-ph scattering processes.

title: Predictions of superconducting properties from chemical bonding interactions
summary: The need for rapid estimates of superconducting critical temperatures, Tc s, is becoming increasingly urgent as first-principles and artificial intelligence based methods enable the exploration of ever-larger and more chemically complex materials spaces. In this context, chemical bonding based quantities have emerged as promising descriptors for predicting superconductivity. To date, these approaches have mainly been developed for hydride superconductors, notably through the networking value, a descriptor based upon the electron localization function, whose topological properties have been found to correlate with Tc . In this perspective, we review and consolidate the method's theory, and we discuss how the estimate of the Tc is achievable within a real-space view. We conclude by proposing a framework that enables Tc prediction for the broad family of conventional superconductors from easily computable intermediate physical quantities.

title: Variational Monte Carlo Study of Superconductivity in a Correlated System with Broken Inversion Symmetry
summary: Unconventional superconductivity in systems with broken inversion symmetry has attracted considerable interest because antisymmetric spin-orbit coupling (ASOC) can strongly affect the spin structure and stability of superconducting states. In this study, we investigate superconductivity in a correlated system with the symmetry of a honeycomb network using the variational Monte Carlo method. We consider a single-band Hubbard model including an on-site Coulomb interaction $U$ and ASOC with coupling strength $λ$, and compare several pairing states with different pairing symmetries. The trial wave functions are constructed from particle-number- and Gutzwiller-projected BCS states. To examine the energetic stability of each pairing state, we calculate the variational energy as a function of the gap amplitude, while optimizing the variational parameter $μ$ and the Gutzwiller parameter $g$ for each gap amplitude. At $U/t = 10$, the $f$-wave state has the lowest variational energy for $λ/t = 0$, whereas the chiral $p$-wave state becomes the most energetically favorable for $λ/t = 0.1$. These results indicate that ASOC strongly affects the competition among superconducting pairing states in the presence of strong electron correlations.

title: Classification and Signatures of Dissipative Quantum Hall-Superconductor Junctions
summary: Fractional quantum Hall (FQH) edges with proximity-induced superconductivity can host parafermionic zero modes (PZMs), making them a promising platform for topological quantum computing. Recent experiments [Gül et al., Phys. Rev. X 12, 021057 (2022)] measured the edge conductance from crossed Andreev reflection (CAR) between counter-propagating FQH edges separated by a narrow superconductor. The observed conductance was small and non-quantized, with two distinct behaviors: some states show temperature-independent conductance, while others show conductance that grows as temperature decreases. We explain these results by dissipation to sub-gap modes in the superconductor and present a phase diagram for the FQH-superconductor junction. We show that for Jain states, temperature-independent non-quantized conductance occurs only in the presence of an integer mode (such as at filling $ν=1\pm\frac{1}{m}$, with odd $m\geq3$) strongly coupled to the dissipative channel. The predicted temperature trends qualitatively agree with the experiment, which shows temperature-independent conductance for $ν=2/3$ and integer states, but not for $ν=1/3$ and $ν=2/5$. We propose comparing $ν=4/3$ and $2/3$ to test the predicted influence of the relative chirality of integer and fractional modes.

summary: Fractional quantum Hall (FQH) edges with proximity-induced superconductivity can host parafermionic zero modes (PZMs), making them a promising platform for topological quantum computing. title: Bypass Transition via the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect
summary: Non-Hermitian skin lattices can directionally amplify propagating signals. Here we show that this amplification and nonlinear feedback together drive a bypass transition to self-sustained motion, familiar from shear flows. A finite local excitation can trigger sustained periodic or chaotic motion while the resting state remains linearly stable. We develop a return-map theory that predicts the triggering threshold, its scaling with directional gain, and the instability governing near-critical dynamics. The threshold decreases exponentially with chain length. Weak noise triggers sustained motion as well, with a characteristic ignition length that grows logarithmically as noise weakens at fixed observation time. Our work establishes a skin-effect route to bypass transitions, opening a new avenue for predicting and controlling nonlinear wave dynamics.

title: Emergent Incompressibility in Polariton Condensates for Scalable XY Spin Simulation
summary: Driven-dissipative polariton networks offer a powerful analog platform for simulating continuous-spin Hamiltonians. However, their practical scalability is fundamentally limited by amplitude-phase coupling and metastable trapping in highly frustrated energy landscapes. Here, we present an \textit{in situ} dual-enhancement mechanism to address these bottlenecks without requiring external site-specific fine-tuning. First, a renormalization-group analysis based on density rescaling shows that higher-order nonlinear loss drives the condensates toward an incompressible regime, intrinsically suppressing amplitude fluctuations and enforcing phase-only dynamics. For macroscopic XY networks (up to 10,000 spins), this phase-amplitude decoupling yields a more than 50-fold reduction in energy, while simultaneously shrinking the standard deviation by a factor of six. More generally, it restores the extensive scaling of the optimized XY energy with system size. Second, to navigate the rugged, nonconvex energy landscape, we introduce weak Hermitian pulses. When implemented through a multistage protocol, these pulses enable repeated escapes from local minima and drive the system to deeper energy minima. Benchmarking shows an increasing advantage with system size, with the polariton simulator outperforming the classical Monte Carlo-SQP baseline in every sampled macroscopic realization. Our work provides a physical framework for scalable polariton analog computing.

title: Gate-reconfigurable Josephson microwave source limited by thermal noise
summary: Josephson junctions are compact on-chip sources of coherent microwave and terahertz radiation, but conventional radiators couple the emission frequency, output power and dissipation through a single bias voltage. Here we demonstrate a gate-reconfigurable Josephson microwave radiator based on a graphene weak link integrated with a separately gated graphene shunt resistor. The bias voltage sets the Josephson frequency, while the local gates tune the Josephson current and the total device resistance, enabling electrostatic control of emitted power at a chosen frequency. The device resolves Josephson harmonics up to fourth order, and its radiation power scales with source current and impedance as expected from a lumped-element circuit model. We further show that the emission linewidth is quantitatively described by Johnson-Nyquist noise at the electron temperature. The linewidth therefore provides an on-chip thermometer under bias, with the resistance-dependent heating captured by a minimal heat-balance model based on Wiedemann-Franz diffusion and electron-phonon coupling.

title: Floquet-Volkov spin polarization in spin-degenerate Antiferromagnets
summary: Periodic driving enables ultrafast control of electronic structures in solids through the formation of photon-dressed Floquet-Bloch states. However, the measured photoemission spectra are influenced not only by these states but also by their interference with Volkov-dressed outgoing photoelectrons. Here, we demonstrate that Floquet-Volkov interference can generate spin-polarized photoemission in a collinear antiferromagnetic Dirac model without spin-orbit coupling (SOC). An in-plane linearly polarized pump preserves $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetry, leaving the Floquet quasienergies spin degenerate. Under near-resonant driving, photon-dressed conduction and valence bands hybridize, producing spin-dependent relative phases that are converted into unequal spin-resolved photoemission intensities through interference between pathways reaching the same Volkov-dressed final state. We analytically identify this interference mechanism and verify it using nonequilibrium Green-function calculations under periodic driving and finite pump-probe pulses. We further demonstrate that rotating the probe polarization can suppress or reverse the spin polarization without modifying the Floquet bands. Our findings establish Floquet-Volkov interference as a route to spin-selective photoemission in driven antiferromagnets without Floquet spin splitting or SOC.

title: The quantized Hall effect knows which way the current flows: mirror covariance and rectification in a laterally asymmetric Hall bar
summary: The quantized Hall effect is the textbook emblem of universality: a resistance fixed by $h/e^2$, apparently indifferent to the shape of the sample, to its edges and to the direction of the current. That indifference is only half true. The plateau value is universal; the plateau is not. In a gate-defined Hall bar with one hard and one soft edge, reversing the current moves the plateau edge, and exchanging the edges reverses the move. We identify the symmetry that forces this. Because a perpendicular field breaks time reversal, the relevant operation is the in-plane $C_2$ rotation; within the self-consistent screening model it gives the covariance relation $R_α[B,V_{\mathrm{conf}}(x),I]=R_α[B,V_{\mathrm{conf}}(-x),-I]$, exact deep in the nonlinear regime and independent of linear response or microscopic reversibility. It predicts a rectification that is odd under exchange of the gate voltages and reverses with the magnetic field. The field-reversal test leaves the frozen lateral disorder untouched, so it holds for a single sample; it has not yet been performed. A further measurement, collapsing one incompressible strip, discriminates between co-directed and chiral pictures of the current. Self-consistent calculations show the soft-edge strip widening from 69 to 106\,nm on current reversal, moving the Hall resistance from 0.940 to $0.999994\,h/2e^2$ within a bounded window in magnetic field. The effect is a gate-tunable vector-product nonreciprocity, not magnetochiral anisotropy.

title: Spin Simulators based on Exciton-Polariton Waveguide Networks
summary: Many NP-hard optimization problems can be mapped onto interacting spin systems, whose ground state encodes the optimal solution. Polaritonic implementations based on gain-dissipative dynamics have recently emerged as promising analog computing platforms owing to their intrinsic parallelism and ultrafast operation. However, existing approaches are hindered by two fundamental limitations: maintaining the homogeneous amplitudes required for faithful problem encoding remains challenging in realistic physical systems, and most architectures are restricted to nearest-neighbour interactions, severely limiting the variety of optimization problems that can be efficiently addressed. We introduce a feasible polaritonic XY simulator based on a reconfigurable waveguide platform that overcomes both limitations. Our approach guarantees amplitude homogeneity while enabling the implementa- tion of arbitrary symmetric coupling matrices, thereby allowing the direct encoding of a wide variety of XY Hamiltonians. These results establish a practical architecture for programmable polaritonic spin simulators and pave the way towards scalable optical hardware for analog optimisation.

title: Electrostatics of Chern junctions in a magnetic field
summary: Electrostatic control is central to the operation of semiconductor junctions made from conventional materials. Here, we theoretically investigate the electrostatic properties of lateral junctions between two-dimensional (2D) Chern semiconductors in a perpendicular magnetic field. The spectral asymmetry of a Chern semiconductor acts as a magnetic-field-induced effective dopant density that is dependent on the Chern number. As a consequence, two regions with different Chern numbers acquire different chemical potentials at charge neutrality, leading to a built-in potential of topological origin across the junction. Using this built-in potential as a boundary condition, we solve the 2D Poisson equation to obtain the electric potential and charge density profiles, as well as the capacitance, of Chern semiconductor junctions. Our results inform the interplay between electronic topology and electrostatics in devices made from 2D materials.

title: Spin swapping mediated by spin-orbital textures in centrosymmetric multiorbital materials
summary: Spin swapping converts a primary spin current into a secondary one by interchanging its flow and spin-polarization directions, attributed to spin-orbit scattering or spin-band splitting. Here we uncover a fundamentally distinct route to spin swapping arising from the orbital degree of freedom in the spin pumping to centrosymmetric multiorbital materials \textit{without spin-band splitting}. When the dynamical proximity ferromagnet injects a longitudinal spin current flowing normal to the interface, spin-orbit-entangled orbital textures redirect the injected spins into longitudinal and transverse orbital currents. Their subsequent conversion back to the spin sector generates transverse spin currents with propagation and polarization directions swapped relative to the primary spin current. The swapping efficiency achieves $50\%$ for Ge and Si. Governed by a fourth-rank tensor constrained by crystalline symmetry and without requiring spin-orbit scattering or inversion symmetry breaking, our finding reveals spin-orbital textures as hidden intermediate channels of spin swapping with unexplored material choices and functionalities.

authors: C. J. L. de la Rosa
title: Hall-Density Collapse as Direct Evidence for Percolative Conduction Onset in Monolayer MoS$_2$ Transistors
comment: 7 pages, 4 figures; Supplemental Material: 12 pages, 7 figures, 1 table. Submitted to Physical Review Letters
summary: The origin of the apparent metal-insulator transition in two-dimensional electron systems remains debated. Using temperature-dependent transport and Hall measurements on industry-relevant MoS$_2$ monolayer FETs with amorphous HfO$_2$ dielectrics, we establish classical percolation as the underlying mechanism. We report two complementary signatures of disorder-driven conduction onset: a temperature-independent Hall-density collapse as a function of absolute gate voltage and a vanishing activation energy at a characteristic carrier density $n_{\mathrm{c}}$, identified as the percolation threshold. These findings identify dielectric-interface disorder, rather than channel quality alone, as the key parameter governing device turn-on. The extracted activation barriers reach values substantially exceeding room-temperature thermal energies, indicating that disorder-driven conduction onset remains relevant well beyond cryogenic transport.
